title: 8-Bit Player
description: herb's top songs remade as 8-bit chiptunes inside a pixel-crisp early-2000s player: two pulse channels, a triangle bass and a noise drum kit play each remake live, while the spectrum analyser, oscilloscope and channel meters read the real output and the ten-band EQ really filters it. Double-click a track, slide the EQ, drag the windows and they snap together.
intent: One period object finished to the edge, now with its own sound: every song in the playlist becomes a short NES-style arrangement synthesised in Web Audio (band-limited pulse waves with duty changes, a stepped triangle, LFSR noise, envelopes and vibrato) on a lookahead clock, and every readout on the skin is drawn from that real signal.
sources: herb reference board: Y2K found-footage montage (fa23bcd4), CRT green terminal text and early-2000s media objects
